newsitem.title: MEXICO: Tropical Storm Andres could damage Mexican coffee.
newsitem.headline: Tropical Storm Andres could damage Mexican coffee.

text.p: The approach of Tropical Storm Andres could damage Mexican coffee plants in the southern state of Chiapas, the Weather Services Corp (WSC) said on Wednesday.
Andres is expected to land on Mexico's southern Pacific coast by about 1800 local (2300 GMT), WSC's Tony Espinola said.
It is also expected to hit Guatemala and Belize.
Oaxaca and Chiapas coffee regions in Mexico could be affected by some possible flooding," he said. "The biggest threat is the heavy rains and floods."

Chiapas' coffee crop is in a key maturing stage after flowering this spring. Harvesting for the 97-98 cycle starts in October in lowland regions around the Tacana volcano that overlooks Tapachula, close to the Guatemala border.
Espinola added that the storm "will not be as destructive as others historically seen in the region."
He said Andres would not affect Mexican coffee plants in key Veracruz and Puebla states and should cause moderate showers in Colombia.
Northern Guatemala and Belize could see flooding, with up to ten inches of rain and possible mudslides, he said, which could threaten Guatemalan coffee plants.
Heavy rains were falling in Chiapas and Oaxaca, and expected to continue throughout Thursday, Mexico's National Weather Service said in its latest storm report.

Andres, the season's first Pacific coast storm front, could pass over Mexican soil later in the week and continue in the Caribbean. There the storm's name would change to Ana, and it would become the season's first Caribbean storm front, Espinola said.
The storm front had been spotted at as close as 25 miles (40 km) from Mexico's Pacific coast heading east-northeast at approximately two miles (one km) per hour, he said.
Winds from the storm were clocked at up to 53 miles (85 km) per hour with gusts at 62 miles (100 km) per hour, the National Weather Service said.
